Render a live cinematic 3D animation of the real rig geometry in a browser (Three.js, served locally, no static-file output) during bundle adjustment as the default live view: cameras as stylized bots at their actual solved pose/orientation glowing by actual current reprojection error, choreographed acts matching the 4 hierarchical-BA stages with title cards, a live per-camera leaderboard, an RMS sparkline, and a finale with final per-camera stats -- replacing the terminal braille view as the default

The live web view launches (server + browser tab) at construction time, before corner detection or per-camera front-end intrinsics have run, and streams real progress through every phase of a config-driven run instead of leaving the browser blank -- live per-camera corner-detection counts during detection, a dedicated stage label through the front-end's per-camera intrinsic fit (no per-iteration callback of its own), the existing BA-stage acts, and live progress through the (now-parallelised) MC-Calib debug-image writers after convergence

Single-camera front-end multi-start seed dispersion runs for every model (no model-class shortcut); a per-model skip was measured unsafe at scale (56/100 RadTan cameras degraded, 0 improved, on thinner synthetic data) and was reverted 2026-07-02. Also covers the same-root-cause cascading seed sensitivity found in ds_msp.rig's own _robust_pinhole pre-seed (a skipped restart there flipped a 16-camera rig's DS fit between the UCM-collapse basin and a genuine xi solution)
Rig front-end Two-start seeding skips the second solve when the model-aware and from-K seeds are byte-identical (a provably lossless deterministic duplicate) instead of always re-solving both

Rig front-end intrinsic pre-calibration and per-frame pose seeding run across cameras in parallel (ProcessPoolExecutor scaling with camera count) with bit-identical results to the serial path irrespective of camera model or distortion level

save_reprojection_images / save_detection_images (MC-Calib-format debug overlay output) run across (camera, frame) tasks in parallel (ThreadPoolExecutor scaling with core count) with bit-identical results to the serial path -- previously fully serial and unparallelised, measured ~12.5s each for 255 images and running silently *after* the bundle adjustment already converged (7x speedup measured, 1.79s parallel vs 12.51s serial, on this repo's real MC-Calib dataset)

Publish a versioned MkDocs Material documentation site (Diataxis tutorial/how-to/reference/explanation sections) alongside the interactive studio, built and link-checked (mkdocs build --strict) in CI so a broken internal link or missing nav reference fails the build instead of silently 404ing on the live site

Every code sample shown on a docs page is a real, independently-runnable file under docs_src/ included via mkdocs's {* docs_src/... *} macro (never hand-copied inline), with a mirrored pytest test asserting the exact values the page shows, and zero dependence on external datasets -- so a reader can trust that what's shown actually runs and is regression-tested

The live web view renders every camera as a glowing sea-creature (procedural, shape keyed by camera model -- octopus/squid/jellyfish/hammerhead/starfish, no borrowed 3D assets) in a procedurally generated pond. An orb's LIVE RANK (not raw error alone) gates how close to the surface it may rise -- only the current top 3 by reprojection error can approach/breach the surface (with real ballistic preview leaps and splashes as the run progresses), 4th place and below are held near the floor regardless of their own error; at the finale the real best-converged camera (lowest final median error) does a real ballistic leap out of the water and settles above the surface (fireworks), while every other camera sinks to the floor. Ambient life: real Reynolds-boid schooling fish (3 shapes, 3 schools each following its own parametric formation curve) that scatter in real predator-avoidance flight when a roaming predator fish comes near, and re-form once it moves away

After the pond finale settles, the live web view transitions into a post-finale "digital twin" reveal: every camera creature swims to its ACTUAL solved T_c_g pose (reusing the same real pose data the live view already carries, not a second computation) and floats above the water, while the board plays back through every real captured frame's solved pose and 3D corner points (reusing report._frame_payload verbatim) start to end on a loop, colored by real per-point reprojection error

During the digital-twin reveal, all cameras and the board-replay points are parented under one rigid "rig root" group; a Blender/CAD-style 3-axis rotation gizmo (TransformControls, rotate mode) lets the user manually re-orient this whole rigid assembly (never touching the underlying T_c_g/T_g_o data) so it visually matches the real room's gravity-down/up orientation, since calibration only ever fixes one reference camera as the origin and has no notion of true up. Purely a live, ephemeral viewing aid -- not persisted

The live browser 3D view is an opt-in capability: `pip install ds-msp[webviewer]` documents/reserves it as an installable extra, and a calib_param.yml `webviewer: true/false` field (default true, matching prior always-on behavior) independently gates whether the run launches it, decoupled from `verbose` (terminal progress) so a headless/CI run can silence one without the other. `--no-webviewer` on the CLI mirrors the config field for the non-config scenario entry point

Every genuinely-boolean calib_param.yml field (fix_intrinsic, save_detection, save_reprojection, verbose, webviewer) accepts the intuitive true/false (also yes/no) form, not just the old, confusing 0/1 numeric convention -- while still accepting 0/1 for backward compatibility with existing config files. Handles a real cv2.FileStorage YAML-parser quirk: an inline `# comment` on the same line as an unquoted bareword value (true/false) is not stripped by the parser the way it is for a numeric 0/1 value, so the parser strips it explicitly. Fields that select between more than two named modes (distortion_model, distortion_per_camera, he_approach) are not booleans and are unchanged

`pip install ds-msp` alone (no repo clone) provides a real `ds-msp-calibrate-rig` console command with feature parity to the git-clone `python scripts/calibrate_rig.py` (which is now a thin wrapper around the same ds_msp.rig.cli:main), including `--init-config`/`--init-intrinsics` template generation -- the calib_param.yml/camera_intrinsics.yml templates ship as real package data (ds_msp/rig/configs/*.yml, resolved via importlib.resources so it works identically whether installed from a wheel, sdist, or editable checkout). tools/check_packaging.py verifies at the pyproject.toml level that the console-script entry point resolves to a real importable target inside a shipped subpackage and that every package-data glob matches real files, so this cannot silently rot

Calibrate a non-overlapping multi-camera rig -- cameras whose boards are never mutually co-observed in any single frame (MC-Calib's ``computeBoardsPairPose``/``init3DObjects`` covisibility-component topology 4-6). The board-fusion front stage keeps every covisibility component as its own ``Object3D`` instead of dropping all but the largest; camera-group hand-eye linking (``rig/handeye.py``) then fuses rigidly-linked objects that share no direct observation (MC-Calib's ``merge3DObjects``) into one rigid object, re-seeds per-frame poses, and re-derives camera groups so the joint BA can identify the inter-camera extrinsic -- iterated until one connected component remains. Validated on a real 2-camera/2-board non-overlapping rig (each camera sees a different, never-co-observed board): 1-camera silent-drop failure fixed to 2 cameras calibrated, 0.80/0.57px RMS, 1.19 m / 178.6 deg recovered extrinsic

Every top-level entry directly under docs/ (file or directory) is explicitly listed in a version-controlled positive allowlist (docs/process/governance/DOCS_TOP_LEVEL_MANIFEST.txt), checked in CI on every PR -- so a new file lands in the public tree only via a deliberate, reviewable one-line addition to the manifest, never silently. This is structurally exhaustive (absence from the list is itself the failure condition, regardless of content or naming) rather than a content pattern scan, and runs as a required CI job on a clean checkout, independent of any local machine's hook configuration

A board observation that is a genuine blunder (e.g. a ChArUco board a different OpenCV build mis-decodes -- correct board, wrong corner ids -- resects to a plausible-but-wrong pose with a low per-board RMS, invisible until composed with the assembled rig) is handled two ways, both available: (1) by default, the robust joint BA (GNC-TLS/Cauchy) down-weights it in the *estimate* -- verified to give the same intrinsics and an extrinsic within 0.1deg/3.5mm as hard-dropping it -- while ``report.py``'s per-camera stats gain ``inlier_rms``/``n_gross`` and a printed note so a correct fit is not misread as a failure just because raw max/rms still counts the blunder, and ``web3d.py``'s live-view depth uses the median (capped) per-camera error so one blunder cannot sink an otherwise-correctly-calibrated camera out of view; (2) an explicit opt-in hard-drop gate, ``calibrate_rig(reproj_gate_px=...)``/``calibrate_scenario(reproj_gate_px=...)`` (MC-Calib's ``ransac_threshold`` semantics -- ``keep it high, remove only strong outliers``), rejects any observation whose reprojection through the assembled rig exceeds the gate and re-solves on the cleaned set; off by default, and NOT auto-wired from ``calibrate_from_config`` (the shipped ``ransac_threshold`` config field remains available for a caller to pass through explicitly, matching the down-weight-first philosophy). Validated on a real rig under a mis-decoding OpenCV build (4.10): max camera error 294.6px -> 2.61px, BA rms 30.6px -> 0.73px, extrinsic unchanged (1.193m / 178.6deg); on a clean build (cv2 5.x, verified again here on the same real Seltos rig) the gate drops 0 observations -- a genuine no-op on clean data

``calib_param.yml``'s ``noise_bound`` field is fully configurable like every other config field: it honors ``--set``/overrides (previously the ONE config field that did not), and a value ``<= 0`` (physically meaningless as a pixel sigma) is the config-layer sentinel for ``None``, disabling GNC-TLS -- so a config file can express 'plain robust IRLS, no GNC-TLS' at all. Previously that was unreachable from any config-driven run: the default ``1.0`` could not be disabled, and ``bundle.refine`` routes to GNC-TLS (ignoring ``robust_kernel``/``gnc_*``) whenever ``noise_bound`` is not ``None``, so those parameters were dead from ``calibrate_from_config``. The pre-existing default (``1.0``, GNC-TLS active) is unchanged for every config that does not mention ``noise_bound``. Origin: the surviving fix from the rejected sparse-studentized-IRLS work (ADR-0014, Rejected -- the studentize capability itself was formally proven on real data to be a no-op-at-real-cost under this pipeline's robust-init regime, and removed).

An opt-in frame-clustered M-estimator sandwich covariance (``clustered_sandwich_covariance``) is available for rig parameter-uncertainty reporting (``bundle.parameter_covariance``, ``calib_param.yml``'s ``report_covariance: true/false``), fixing a measured 4-9x real-data under-coverage of the existing (unclustered) sandwich covariance: per-corner scores were treated as independent when corners from the same synchronized board placement (pooled across cameras) share correlated board-pose noise. Clustering the meat by frame id (bread unchanged; Liang-Zeger/Cameron-Miller clustered-sandwich form, small-cluster scalar correction c = [G/(G-1)]*[(N-1)/(N-K)], df = G-1) closes a synthetic known-correlation Monte-Carlo under-coverage of 6.2x (std) / 38x (variance) down to a 0.98x coverage ratio (0.98-1.10x under a contaminated/robust refit). Formally proven honest on real data by a 200-replicate cluster bootstrap (resample the 33 real Seltos board placements with replacement, refit, compare each estimator's single-fit predicted std to the bootstrap-measured empirical std): median coverage ratio naive 0.147 (~7x overconfident), unclustered sandwich 0.275 (~3.6x overconfident), frame-clustered 1.136 (honest, slightly conservative). The user-facing output therefore reports ONLY the frame-clustered estimator (per-camera ``extrinsic_std``/``intrinsic_std``, tangent layout rotation-first: ``[dw(3) rad, dt(3) scene units]``); the two proven-overconfident estimators remain in ``ds_msp/core/covariance.py`` as documented test baselines only, never shown where a smaller std could be mistaken for a better calibration.

An observability audit of the rig calibration runs by DEFAULT (``audit_gate: warn``; ``off``/``refuse`` selectable from config or ``--set``) and turns near-null directions of the gauge-fixed weighted BA Hessian into NAMED, actionable findings. Math: van der Sluis diagonal equilibration (Numer. Math. 14, 1969) of ``H = J^T W J`` to unit diagonal -- REQUIRED because J's columns mix physical units (px/rad, px/length, px/px, px/1), making raw eigenvalues and eigenvector components unit artefacts; measured on a healthy 3-camera rig cond(H)=1.7e11 vs cond(H_hat)=2.1e6. Two-tier thresholds locked from MEASURED spectra (2026-07-18 characterization): structural degeneracies (gauge modes, planar focal<->xi coupling) sit at equilibrated-eigenvalue ratios <=1e-10 while the softest healthy directions sit >=1e-5, so critical=1e-6 / soft=1e-3 sit inside a measured ~6-order gap -- not hand-tuned. Findings name the known fisheye degeneracy signatures with capture advice (focal<->distortion planar coupling -> add tilt; outer-FOV params + empty periphery annulus -> capture near edges; weak frames; weak extrinsics; degenerate capture motion; global gauge = bug detector), corroborated by Hessian-free coverage stats (equal-area radial occupancy, board-normal orientation-tensor tilt diversity). Verified: silent (n_weak=0) on a well-conditioned 3D-target rig; EXACTLY 6 global-gauge findings when the reference camera is deliberately unfixed (positive control); no-tilt planar DS capture names fx,fy<->xi at ratio 1.8e-13; centered-board capture flags periphery with occupancy 0%; naming proven unit-invariant only under equilibration (m->mm test). ``refuse`` raises instead of returning a silently under-constrained calibration -- the failure class where the solver's Cholesky jitter rescues a near-singular system and returns a confident-looking answer. No calibration library ships a named, gated observability diagnostic (gap audit 2026-07-18; Calibration Wizard ICCV 2019 / AprilCal IROS 2013 are standalone guidance tools).

An opt-in (``certify: true``) a-posteriori GLOBAL-OPTIMALITY certificate for the rig's extrinsic-rotation backbone: the per-view robust-PnP rotations (``ObjectObs.T_c_o``) define a weighted chordal rotation-synchronization problem on the bipartite camera x board-placement graph; the BA rotations are refined to a first-order critical point of that cost and the Lagrangian-dual certificate ``S = L - Lambda`` is checked by eigendecomposition (Eriksson et al. CVPR 2018 Lemma 3.2; Rosen et al. SE-Sync IJRR 2019 Thm 7; construction also shipped in GTSAM ShonanAveraging -- cited prior art; the novelty is surfacing it as a user-facing calibration-trust output, a first among calibration libraries per the 2026-07-18 gap audit). Soundness (audited against the fetched papers): a PASS proves global optimality of the weighted chordal cost on this measurement graph with NO false positives regardless of relaxation tightness; errors are ONE-SIDED (a FAIL is inconclusive); it does NOT certify PnP-input correctness, translations, or intrinsics -- stated verbatim in the output message. Convention is load-bearing and sign-tested: frame-from-world nodes ``Z_c=R_c_g``,``Z_t=R_g_o^T`` with ``R_ct = Z_c Z_t^T`` (the transposed convention mis-poses the problem SILENTLY -- caught by the mandatory zero-noise d(BA,chordal)=0 test; first wiring measured 58deg). Gross PnP measurement outliers are trimmed and REPORTED (never silently kept nor dropped): pass 1 scores each edge by min(residual at BA config, residual at refined solution) -- outlier only if inconsistent with BOTH, so a wrong-basin camera's edges survive (evidence kept) and good edges of a dragged frame node survive; trim at max(6 x median, 15deg) from measured separation (real inlier medians 0.38-2.3deg vs outliers 17-177deg); pass 2 certifies the cleaned graph. Outputs: ``eta`` (scale-relative min eigenvalue, tol 1e-6 -- gauge zeros ~1e-15, planted wrong basin -0.13), suboptimality ``gap_bound`` (3n|lambda_min|), ``d_cam_deg``/``d_frame_deg`` (BA-vs-certified distance split by node type; cameras are the calibration output so ``ba_consistent`` = d_cam <= max(3 x median residual, 0.5deg)), ``outlier_edges`` (cam+frame+deg, worst first). Verified: noise-free certifies at d=0; chordal-grad FD-checked <=1e-5 (jac gate); planted non-global critical point REFUSED; planted 60deg-wrong camera POSITIVELY DETECTED as WRONG-BASIN WARNING (d_cam=57.3deg vs ~1deg residuals) with its edges NOT trimmed; planted single 92deg-flipped measurement trimmed + named while still certifying consistent. Real data (2026-07-18): Seltos CERTIFIED+consistent d_cam 0.34deg with 1 named outlier (was a FALSE wrong-basin warning pre-trim); MC-Calib 8-cam fisheye CERTIFIED+consistent eta=-1.7e-15 d_cam 6.2deg with 12 named outliers incl. five 160-177deg near-antipodal fisheye-PnP flips, the ADR-0013 failure mode (was NOT-certified eta=-1.29e-6 pre-trim).

The final rig-calibration result is delivered as ONE comprehensive report rendered from a single JSON-safe data dict (``report.full_report_data``) so the terminal output and the persisted files cannot drift apart: capture summary (cameras/objects/frames/observations/corners), per-camera reprojection-error distribution table + PASS/WARN/FAIL verdict, calibrated intrinsics per camera (every model parameter, with 1-sigma bounds from the frame-clustered sandwich covariance when ``report_covariance`` is on, and a pointer to enable it when off), extrinsics relative to the reference camera (T_c_ref, camera center, baseline, so3_log rotation angle/axis, 1-sigma rotation/translation RSS), the trust layer (observability audit + optimality certificate, or how to enable them), reference comparisons, and the output-file listing. Whenever a save directory is set the SAME content is persisted as ``calibration_report.txt`` (the terminal text verbatim, ANSI-stripped) and ``calibration_report.json`` (the full machine-readable dict, strict JSON: non-finite floats -> null). Verified: saved txt == rendered text byte-for-byte; JSON round-trips equal to the source dict; colored terminal render differs from the file only by ANSI escapes; section numbers reproduce ground truth on an exactly-consistent synthetic rig (fx 520, baseline 0.15, rot 8 deg).
